title: Tool execution loop: multi-tool chaining, tool-result injection, and recursion guards
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a robust tool execution loop in the Core API to enable multi-tool chaining, deterministic injection of tool results into the model context, and runtime recursion/loop guards. This ticket covers the API contract, runtime behavior, compatibility with existing structured-output/tool-calling features, observability hooks, and rollout plan. The goal is to allow a single request to orchestrate multiple tool calls (sync and async), have tool outputs injected as structured tokens/objects for subsequent steps, and prevent runaway recursion or repeated cycles caused by model->tool->model loops.
conformance_notes: Must remain backward-compatible with current function/tool-calling fields. New fields must be optional and default to legacy semantics.
acceptance_criteria: API exposes 'tool_chain' field allowing an ordered list of tool invocations with per-step options (timeout, retry, upload refs).
Tool outputs can be injected into the next model prompt as structured payloads (JSON objects) or as synthetic text tokens depending on 'injection_mode'.
Maximum recursion depth and cycle detection configurable per-request and enforced by runtime (default depth=5).
Streaming responses reflect interim tool call events (tool.started, tool.stdout/chunk, tool.completed) using existing streaming envelope format.
Compatibility layer transforms older 'function_call' requests to equivalent single-step 'tool_chain' when provided.
Unit and integration tests cover sync tool success, async tool completion after model response, tool failures, timeouts, and cycle detection.
Observability exposes per-tool latency, token delta, and error/retry counts in Console trace and token-level breakdown.
implementation_steps: Design: finalize API schema for 'tool_chain' and 'injection_mode' (embed/json/text).
Runtime: extend execution loop to accept multi-step chain and orchestrate tool adapters.
Safety: implement recursion depth counter, seen-tool-sequence hash for cycle detection, and per-request timeout.
Compatibility: add adapter to map legacy 'function_call' to 'tool_chain' with single entry.
Streaming: add event envelopes for tool lifecycle and wire through existing streaming socket.
Testing: write unit tests for tool adapters and e2e tests using the sandbox tool runner.
Docs: update API reference, example playbooks, and SDK helper methods (py/ts).
Rollout: feature-flag behind 'tool_chain_v1' with gradual rollout and telemetry gating.
review_notes: 2026-03-04 - Design review (Lena Zhao): requested clearer semantics for 'injection_mode' and examples showing when to use 'embed' vs 'json'.
2026-03-06 - Security (Marco Ruiz): flagged need for KMS-scoped secrets when tool outputs contain PII; added security_review_required.
2026-03-10 - SDK (Nora Patel): requested helper that converts tool results to validated structured schema before injection.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ravi: spike complete. PoC runs two chained tools (geo_lookup -> pricing_service) with JSON injection working in dev cluster.
2026-03-05 - QA: found intermittent timeouts when tool steps are chained with long cold-start adapters; added retry/backoff guidance.
2026-03-12 - Ravi: implemented cycle detection using rolling hash of tool ids + input fingerprints. Need loadtest to validate false-positive rate.
2026-03-13 - PM (Ivy Chen): prioritize dashboards for per-tool cost attribution in Console before broad rollout.
tests: Unit: tool adapter mocks for sync/async; validate injection modes and error propagation.
Integration: full request flow using sandbox tools with streaming events captured and validated.
Load: 1000 parallel chained requests with average chain length 3 to verify latency SLOs and guard behavior.
Fuzz: randomized chains to verify cycle detection doesn't block legitimate non-repeating sequences.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable feature-flag for 5% of production traffic, run synthetic tests and compare error rates.
Stage 2 (beta): enable for customers opted into Beta with telemetry; collect usage patterns and edge cases.
Stage 3 (GA): default-on but maintain compatibility mode for legacy 'function_call' requests for 3 months.
Rollback: if tool-related errors exceed 0.5% of requests or average p95 latency increases >20%, rollback flag and auto-failover to single-tool legacy path.
